Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.

High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Dhar, Judge
 Order

The appellant has challenged award dated 28.06.2019 passed by the Commissioner under Employees Compensation Act (ALC), Jammu (hereinafter referred to as the Commissioner),
whereby an amount of Rs. 10,69,124/- along with interest has been awarded as compensation in favour of the claimants/respondent nos. 1 to 4.
02.

It appears that respondent nos. 1 to 4 had filed a claim petition before the Commissioner seeking compensation on account of death of Mohan Lal, who happens to be husband of respondent no. 1 and father of respondent nos. 2 to 4.

It was claimed that death of the deceased had taken place,
while he was performing duties of a driver with vehicle bearing no. JK02U/7881 that was owned by respondent no. 5 herein.
The accident is alleged to have taken place on 28.08.2012 at National Highway, Ramsoo at about 8:25 PM.

The age of the deceased was stated to be 35 years and his monthly income was stated to be Rs. 10,000/-.
03.
The petition was resisted by the appellant Insurance Company, by filing a reply thereto.

In its reply, the appellant Insurance Company contended that the deceased had not suffered injuries due to the alleged accident nor his death had taken place during and in the course of employment of the insured.

It was further claimed that the vehicle in question was being driven in contravention of the Senior Divisional Manager vs Neelam Kumari And Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43564113/
1 terms and conditions of the policy of insurance inter-alia for the reason that the deceased was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the relevant time.

entities.text: Senior Divisional Manager vs Neelam Kumari And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Commissioner on the basis of the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues.
"a) Whether the deceased "Mohan Lal" falls under the definition of "employee" as prescribed under the provisions of The E.C. Act, 1923?
O.P.P b) Whether the deceased met with an accident during and in the course of his employment for his employer i.e n/a no. l?
O.P.P c) What was the age and wages of the deceased at the time of accident?

O.P.P.
d) Whether the vehicle bearing registration no. JK02U-7881, involved in accident was driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, at the time under reference?
e) Relief?

O.P. Parties"
04.

After recording evidence of the parties, the learned Commissioner came to the conclusion that the deceased had died during and in the course of his employment with respondent no. 5 herein,
while driving the heavy goods vehicle in question.

The Commissioner assessed the income of the deceased as Rs. 8,000/- and his age was taken as 35 years and thereafter computed the amount of compensation of Rs. 7,88,240/- in favour of the claimants, while deciding the issue with regard to the validity of the driving license of the deceased.

The Commissioner came to the conclusion that there was no evidence on record to show that the driving license was not valid as on the date of the accident and, as such, there was no violation of terms and conditions of the policy of insurance.

05. Heard and considered.
06.
Learned counsel for the appellant has assailed the award primarily on two grounds.

One that the driving license of the deceased was not valid and there was evidence on record before the Commissioner to show that the driving license of the deceased authorized him only to drive a light motor vehicle and not a heavy goods vehicle and that this evidence has been ignored by the learned Commissioner.

Secondly, it has been contended that the vehicle in question had been sold by its owner prior to the accident and, as such, there was no relationship of the employee and employer between the deceased and the owner of vehicle in question as on the date of the accident.
It is being urged that this aspect of the matter has also been ignored by the learned Commissioner.

07. If we have a look at the record of the learned Commissioner, it is revealed that photocopy of the driving license of the deceased, which is on record, shows that it is endorsed for HGV meaning thereby that the deceased was authorized to drive a heavy goods vehicle.
Thus, the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the deceased was not holding an effective driving license, is not supported by the record on the file of the Commissioner.

So far as the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the vehicle in question had been sold prior to the date of the accident Senior Divisional Manager vs Neelam Kumari And Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43564113/
2 is concerned, it is to be noted that this contention was not even raised by the appellant Insurance Company before the Commissioner and in fact, there is no evidence on record of the file of the learned Commissioner to even remotely suggest that the offending vehicle had been transferred by its owner prior to the accident.
08.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the forgoing reasons, no substantial question of law arises in this appeal for determination by this Court.
The appeal lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed.
The award amount deposited in the Registry/the Commissioner shall be released in favour of the claimants/respondents.
